ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Low-intensity pixels (dark grey/black) dominate approximately 85-90% of the visible fluke surface; high-intensity pixels (white/light grey) are concentrated in localized medial clusters and linear streaks.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-contrast white mottled clusters are located in the medial region of both lobes. Distinct white linear streaks radiate from the medial-superior areas towards the distal tips, with higher density and length observed on the right lobe compared to the left.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central notch with an estimated interior angle of 75 degrees and significant depth relative to the horizontal axis of the fluke.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: The trailing edge boundary exhibits high-frequency, low-amplitude serrations; several larger, irregular notches (macro-serrations) are visible on the distal half of the right lobe's trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges follow a sigmoidal trajectory: concave curvature immediately adjacent to the median notch, transitioning to convex curvature towards the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized circular high-intensity pixel clusters (~5-12 pixels in diameter) are visible on the medial-superior portion of the right lobe and near the distal tip of the left lobe, consistent with barnacle attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Highly visible parallel white linear disruptions (rake marks) occur across the right lobe, radiating from the center towards the edge; scattered unaligned linear marks are present on the left medial surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive rake mark scarring on the right lobe; irregular trailing edge contour suggesting minor historical tissue loss or nicks.
other_distinctive_markers: A small, dark, localized protrusion is visible on the superior boundary (leading edge) of the left lobe, approximately mid-way between the median notch and the distal tip.
